title: DARPA BTO Office-Wide BAA HR001126S0003 — Phase 65 Agriculture and bioeconomy review
summary: Phase 65 reviews this primary record as part of the Agriculture and bioeconomy reporting pack. The BTO solicitation seeks biological research that can protect warfighters and create operational capabilities. The office spans AI-enabled biology, threat detection, medical countermeasures, human performance, biological manufacturing, resilient infrastructure, and sensing.
key_findings: BTO treats biology as an engineering and manufacturing domain as well as a health domain.
Research areas connect detection, countermeasures, tactical care, and human performance.
Biological production and resilient infrastructure create scale-up and supply-chain dependencies.
why_it_matters: Which records connect research and authorization to field adoption, production, resilience, water exposure, and comparable crop outcomes? This record supplies one bounded part of that evidence chain; it is not a substitute for the pack's downstream records. It reveals how biological discovery becomes a national-security production, sensing, logistics, and resilience problem.
ftfn_relevance: Extends the bioeconomy topic from laboratory results into manufacturing and operational systems.
Supports monitoring dual-use infrastructure, biosecurity, and scale-up constraints.
evidence_limits: Inclusion in a Phase 65 reporting pack does not advance a Phase 64 matrix cell or establish an operating outcome.
The BAA is a research-interest document, not evidence that any proposed capability works.
Sensitive or classified follow-on work may not be visible in the public record.
